title: A repartition that didn't stick
prompt: Someone wants both cores to work on `api_requests`, so they wrote this. What does it actually print? Type each line on its own line.
program:
# Spread the requests over 4 partitions so both cores get work
api_requests.repartition(4)
print(api_requests.rdd.getNumPartitions())
print(api_requests.count())
hints: Does `repartition` change the DataFrame you call it on, or give back a new one?
The new DataFrame isn't stored in any variable here.
`api_requests` was read from one small file, and that hasn't changed.
explanation: `repartition(4)` gives back a new DataFrame, but the program throws it away. `api_requests` itself still has the single partition it was read with, and still 12 rows. The fix is to keep the result: `spread = api_requests.repartition(4)`.
